claims.content: To adhere to Correlation Restrictions that inhibit automatic correlation when Identity conflicts or different Mode II codes exist.

scope_contract.goal_statement: To adhere to Correlation Restrictions that inhibit automatic correlation when Identity conflicts or different Mode II codes exist.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: The C2 JU manages track identity classification by adhering to a correlation restriction that inhibits automatic correlation for a track when an identity conflict or a different Mode II code condition exists.
scope_contract.start_boundary: A track's identity information is available to the C2 JU for correlation, and an identity-conflict or different-Mode-II-code condition exists.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The applicable correlation restriction is adhered to and automatic correlation is inhibited under the identified condition.
in_scope_actions: Manage track identity classification by adhering to correlation restrictions that inhibit automatic correlation when identity conflicts or different Mode II codes exist.
excluded_adjacent_actions: Assuming R² for an IU when local sensor data is correlated.
Accepting retransmission field values upon assuming R² for a previously-reported track.
Distinguishing exercise-associated live tracks from other live tracks.
Electing to accept eligible identity, category, or exercise-indicator changes from PPLI reports.
variant_dimensions: Whether the condition inhibiting automatic correlation is an identity conflict or a different Mode II code.

missing_aspects: The cited evidence card (EC-G-008) supports the action of adhering to restrictions and inhibiting correlation based on specific conditions. However, it does not explicitly state the high-level goal is 'To manage track identity classification'. While related, this phrasing adds a scope ('manage classification') not strictly present in the provided summary text of the evidence card.

claims.content: C2 JU

The C2 JU has received remote IFF/SIF data (e.g., Mode I, II, III, or IV) and possesses own-unit data in one of the documented states ('NO DATA', 'VALID NON-CURRENT DATA', or 'VALID CURRENT DATA') sufficient to initiate identity-conflict/difference-resolution processing.

Before the use case begins, an automatic-correlation-inhibiting identity condition exists for two tracks: either (a) the local/remote data held indicates an Identity (ID) difference that constitutes a conflict, or (b) the two tracks have different Mode II codes with the local Mode II code current; in either case, the applicable correlation restriction is not inhibited by parameter.
During correlation processing, the C2 JU detects that two tracks have an Identity difference that constitutes a conflict or have different Mode II codes with the local Mode II code current.
C2 JU identifies the applicable correlation-inhibiting condition for the tracks: an Identity conflict or different Mode II codes with the local Mode II code current.
C2 JU determines that the automatic correlation restriction has not been inhibited by a system initialization parameter and operator-selectable capability.
C2 JU adheres to the applicable Correlation Restriction and does not automatically correlate the two tracks.

claims.content: Diverges from main flow Step 3 when conflicting IDs are the only correlation restriction: the operator shall be alerted to take one of the following actions: (a) Change the local ID or the Exercise Indicator and ID, thereby allowing automatic correlation; (b) Transmit an ID Difference Report, thereby allowing automatic correlation if the remote ID or Exercise Indicator and ID is changed; (c) Confirm the restriction, thereby inhibiting the correlation; or (d) Conduct voice coordination to resolve the situation.

Alternative path: Initiate Difference Report message
Alternative path: Change local data to match remote (with Mode II exception)
Alternative path: Decorrelate data and assign new track number

claims.content: If the R² JU identifies that an ID conflict exists, the operator shall be alerted and the local ID data shall continue to be reported in the appropriate surveillance message, with the Identity Difference Indicator set to value 1; the conflict will be resolved by manual means.

If the Identity Difference Indicator is set to value 1 for a non-R² unit, the unit may either: (a) follow the actions in Table 4.7-2 while inhibiting transmission of the J7.0 (ACT = 1) message until a surveillance message is received with the Identity Difference Indicator reset to value 0; or (b) take no action with respect to the reported ID, with an operator alert provided as a system option.

When an operator receives an IFF/SIF data conflict alert, the operator has the following manual actions available for attempting resolution of the difference: (1) update local data manually or verify automatic inputs; (2) initiate a J7.5 (ACT = 0) Clear IFF/SIF message (any mode); (3) initiate a J7.5 (ACT = 1) IFF/SIF Difference Report message (any mode); (4) change local data to agree with remote data except in the case of Mode II code; (5) decorrelate the local data from the remote data, causing assignment of a new track number to the local data; and (6) clear the operator alert (any mode).

If any of the manual resolution actions result in resolution of the ID conflict, the track number to be retained shall be tested for decorrelation in accordance with paragraph 4.4.4.3.2a before executing the correlation, except that the test shall be conducted only once.

When erroneous codes are detected and there are no other valid codes available or changes are inhibited (as in Mode II code reporting), the system shall have a capability to delete or clear the erroneous codes so that the interface can return to a No Data status for the specified track and its corresponding mode(s).

When the Identity Difference Indicator is set to value 1, if the R² JU is directed to automatically reject the remote ID, the system shall discard the message and the track shall continue to be reported with local data.
Automatic correlation of the two tracks is inhibited due to the Identity conflict, adhering to the applicable Correlation Restriction.
Automatic correlation of the two tracks is inhibited due to different Mode II codes (with local code current), adhering to the applicable Correlation Restriction.

missing_aspects: The claim asserts a 'successful handling' phase which is not described in the evidence; the evidence only supports the immediate inhibition action.

quality_flags.detail: [exceptionflow_exit_coverage] The non-R² unit branch includes an option to 'take no action' with only an optional operator alert. This option ends in a no-op/optional alert and does not provide a clear outcome such as return to Main Flow, termination, handoff, or terminal failure/prevention state. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Explicit evidence that taking no action leaves the ID conflict unresolved and the reported ID unchanged.))

[trigger_preconditions_coverage] The Trigger assumes correlation processing is already underway ('During correlation processing, the C2 JU detects...'), but no Precondition states that the two tracks are undergoing correlation processing or that C2 JU is performing it. Without this state, the detection event cannot occur. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (The cited cards do not support the claim that specifically two tracks are involved; EC-PC-014 refers to all tracks and IUs tested for correlation.))

[trigger_preconditions_coverage] The Trigger assumes correlation processing is already underway ('During correlation processing, the C2 JU detects...'), but no Precondition states that the two tracks are undergoing correlation processing or that C2 JU is performing it. Without this state, the detection event cannot occur.

inconsistency_hints: The Trigger can start for either an Identity-conflict condition or a different-Mode-II condition, but Preconditions only explicitly asserts the different-Mode-II condition. Claim 0 only says the C2 JU has data sufficient to initiate identity-conflict/difference-resolution processing; it does not state that an Identity conflict between two tracks already exists before the detection Trigger.

The exception branch for an R² JU ID conflict only states that the operator is alerted and local ID data continues to be reported with Identity Difference Indicator set to 1. It does not specify a clear outcome such as returning to a Main Flow step, terminating or handing off, or an explicit terminal failure/prevention state.
